title: Small flow, long duration
hook: A millilitre-per-minute amount repeats many more times in a day than in an hour.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Convert a small continuous flow to hourly and daily volumes.

misconception: A small rate remains a small total regardless of duration.
objective: Convert a small continuous flow to hourly and daily volumes.

claims.text: A hypothetical constant 5mL/min flow continues for either one hour or one day. Scaled model; illustrative constant flow; 24h/day; 1000mL/L.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Flow=5mL/min, A=7.2L and B=0.3L. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",["*","x",1440],1000]; B=["/",["*","x",60],1000]; x denotes Flow. At x=5, A=7.2, B=0.3; recall at x=8: B=0.48. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions.

claims.text: A day contains 1,440 minutes; an hour contains sixty. Multiply by the relevant minute count and convert millilitres to litres. A small rate and a long duration belong in the same calculation.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",["*","x",1440],1000]; B=["/",["*","x",60],1000]; x denotes Flow. At x=5, A=7.2, B=0.3; recall at x=8: B=0.48. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: A hypothetical constant 5mL/min flow continues for either one hour or one day. Change only Flow to 8mL/min. What is B (One-hour) now? Correct: 0.48L. Use B's stated rule with Flow=8mL/min: it gives 0.48L. A day contains 1,440 minutes; an hour contains sixty. Multiply by the relevant minute count and convert millilitres to litres. A small rate and a long duration belong in the same calculation.

recall.question: A hypothetical constant 5mL/min flow continues for either one hour or one day. Change only Flow to 8mL/min. What is B (One-hour) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Flow=8mL/min: it gives 0.48L. A day contains 1,440 minutes; an hour contains sixty. Multiply by the relevant minute count and convert millilitres to litres. A small rate and a long duration belong in the same calculation.

safety.assumptions: A hypothetical constant 5mL/min flow continues for either one hour or one day.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
